sources.entry: asciimatics - A package to create full-screen text UIs (from interactive forms to ASCII animations).

summary.one_liner: Asciimatics is a cross-platform Python package for building full-screen text UIs, from interactive forms and widgets to ASCII animations.
keywords: make a text interface in python
summary.what_it_does: Provides a single cross-platform Screen class for low-level console work: coloured and styled text, cursor positioning, non-blocking keyboard input, mouse input where the terminal supports it, and detecting console resizes. On top of that it offers higher-level APIs for anti-aliased ASCII line drawing, converting images (including JPEG and GIF) to ASCII, and animation effects such as sprites, particle systems, stars and banners. It also includes text UI widgets such as buttons, text boxes and radio buttons. Scenes group effects and are played by the Screen. The README shows a short hello-world example and an animated title example, and points to a samples directory and online docs for more.
use_cases: build a full-screen terminal form or contact list
animated ASCII title screens or demos
read keyboard and mouse input in a console app
how_to_run: Windows users not using pip: install pywin32
Save the hello-world example from the README as a .py file and run it with python
Run the sample scripts from the project samples directory with python
notable: Single cross-platform Screen class covering Windows, macOS and Linux consoles
Includes high-level widgets and effects, not just low-level drawing
Image to ASCII conversion with JPEG and GIF support
Samples directory and recorded gallery of demos
caveats: Python 3 only for current releases; the last version supporting Python 2 is v1.14
Relies on a working curses implementation on non-Windows platforms
Windows without pip needs pywin32 installed manually
